notes: Reached via Chrome (Shopify store, no WAF/challenge). robots.txt has no Claude-specific Disallow: it names UCP/MCP for agent commerce and 'checkouts are for humans' but Allow: / for crawling. Tree came from the site's own header 'FURNITURE' mega-menu (extracted from the live DOM), whose children are Coffee Table, Console, Dining Table, End Table, Mirror, Seating, Shelf, Storage. Mirror was excluded (belongs to the Wall Decor/Mirrors task, not Furniture, per project scope). Every remaining node was verified by same-origin fetch of /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 from the loaded page (all returned well under the 250 cap, i.e. complete single-page enumerations). The site publishes NO rendered product-count header anywhere on its collection pages (checked live on /collections/seating: only a '0 ITEMS' cart badge, no listing count) so full-catalog enumeration is the qty source for every row, per Rule 4 priority 3. Two site-only 'all furniture' aggregator views (collections/furniture=135, collections/furniture-no-sale=120) and one redundant table-aggregator tag (collections/tables=12, not present in the mega-menu and fully overlapping with Coffee Table/Dining Table) were excluded as non-leaf/duplicate per the URL hierarchy rule. A separate 'desk' collection (34 items) sits in a different, non-Furniture menu block (grouped with Mug/Organiser/Stationery) and is overwhelmingly desk ACCESSORIES, not desk furniture (only 1 SKU in the entire 240-product catalog carries product_type 'Desk') - excluded. Two mislabeling traps matched the prior Home-Decor pass's findings for this same store: 'Step Bar (Wall Mounted)' is product_type-tagged 'Mirror' but is actually a wall-mounted bar/console unit and was kept as furniture inside Console; 'Parallel Lines Boxes #3' is titled 'Boxes' but its body_html ('solid wood and roomy cabinets... a storage piece') confirms it is a real cabinet, kept inside Shelf. Storage (16 items) is a sibling nav node that heavily cross-lists items already counted in Shelf/Console (by design, tag-based) plus one exclusive new SKU ('Yin Yang Cabinet') and one non-furniture item ('Basic Key Hook & Organiser', a wall/door key hook) - the literal site count of 16 is kept as qty with a flag on the one non-furniture item, since it is what the URL actually displays and 15/16 are genuine furniture. No parent/child duplication: only the deepest sibling leaf nodes are recorded, all as direct children of the Furniture department (no intermediate grouping level exists on this site, so no is_group rows are needed).
